Date: 2025-12-20
Start: 15:30 PST
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Sofia Martinez (Redwood AE), Daniel Kim (Redwood SE), Priya Rao (Redwood Content), Aisha Patel (Lumina Head of ML), Dr. Marco Ruiz (Lumina CTO), Elaine Chen (Lumina Marketing)
summary: Informal podcast-style customer interview. Lumina Health discusses how they adopted Redwood Inference for production LLM features in triage summarization and patient communication automation. Topics include technical wins (latency, cost), deployment choices (Dedicated for PHI workloads), security requirements, and suggested talking points for the public case study. Agreed next steps: share raw audio, approve testimonial copy, and publish edited episode in early January.
transcript:
[00:00] Sofia (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining \u001f this is just a casual recording for a podcast-style customer interview, feel free to be candid. We are recording, audio levels look good.
[00:12] Aisha (Lumina): Yep sounds good on our side, hi all. Happy to be here.
[00:18] Daniel (Redwood): Great. Quick intros \u001f I'm Daniel from Redwood, infra/SE team, I worked directly with Aisha on the pilot.
[00:26] Marco (Lumina): Marco here, CTO, been following the rollout. Elaine from marketing is with us too.
[00:33] Elaine (Lumina): Hi hi.
[00:35] Sofia (Redwood): Cool. Aisha, maybe start with a bit of background \u001f what problem were you solving when you first evaluated Redwood?
[00:45] Aisha (Lumina): Sure. So at Lumina we were looking to automate post-visit patient summaries and triage messages, the problem was twofold \u001f scale and compliance. We had a small in-house model but inference costs were high and latency inconsistent, and then PHI obviously made us cautious about where inference runs.
[01:05] Sofia (Redwood): Right, and I remember the first POC \u001f you ran both hosted and our Dedicated offering in parallel?
[01:12] Aisha (Lumina): Yeah we did. Hosted for initial speed of getting up, but we eventually moved the PHI workflows to Dedicated inside our VPC. That solved our audit log and KMS key control requirements, and we still use hosted for lower-sensitivity tasks.
[01:29] Daniel (Redwood): Was the switch to Dedicated painful? Any surprises?
[01:33] Aisha (Lumina): Not too bad. There were some network config bits and our security team wanted extra validation, but Redwood's private deployment checklist and the on-prem package docs helped a lot. A tiny bit of back and forth about RBAC mapping and key rotation policies.
[01:49] Marco (Lumina): The thing that sold us was predictable latency under load. We had a live demo where we pushed a 200-concurrent request test and your Dedicated pool kept p95 latency stable, that was convincing.
[01:59] Daniel (Redwood): Nice, thanks for calling that out, we tuned the batching and KV cache for that workload.
[02:05] Elaine (Lumina): From a marketing POV, the ROI story was huge \u001f the automation reduced manual summarization time by about 60% and cut turnaround from hours to minutes, so patients get faster follow-up.
[02:18] Sofia (Redwood): Love that stat. Aisha, can you share a bit about model and quality \u001f were you using open models or a tuned variant?
[02:27] Aisha (Lumina): We started on an open Llama-derived model, then moved to a quantized 4-bit variant recommended by Redwood for production. Quality held up once we adjusted prompts and added a simple reranker \u001f output drift was our main concern so we set up evals and regression alerts.
[02:45] Daniel (Redwood): Did you leverage Redwood Optimize suggestions for batching/quantization?
[02:49] Aisha (Lumina): Yes, the Optimize report was handy. We used it to set autoscaling and batching thresholds \u001f ended up reducing token cost by roughly 30% without impacting p95.
[02:58] Marco (Lumina): There was a bit of internal debate about using OpenAI vs self-hosted options like Anthropic or Bedrock but the cost math and control over PHI pushed us to Redwood.
[03:12] Sofia (Redwood): Good point. For listeners who care about compliance, did you need SOC2/ISO evidence and did Redwood's docs suffice?
[03:20] Aisha (Lumina): We required SOC 2 Type II and an attestation on key handling. Redwood's security packet plus the KMS integration notes were fine; our auditors had a few follow-up questions but everything closed.
[03:34] Elaine (Lumina): Quick aside \u001f can we capture a couple of soundbites for the case study? Like \"Reduced turnaround from hours to minutes\" and \"Predictable p95 latency under load\" \u001f are you okay with that, Aisha?
[03:46] Aisha (Lumina): Yes, that's fine. We'll need final copy for legal signoff but happy to provide short quotes.
[03:53] Sofia (Redwood): Great, we'll draft those and send them. Priya from our content team will shepherd approvals.
[03:59] Priya (Redwood): Hi everyone, just jumping in \u001f planning to do a 3-4 minute highlight reel and a longer 20-25 minute episode with more technical detail. Any preferences?
[04:12] Elaine (Lumina): Both sounds good. We'll want the technical deep-dive for engineering folks and the short one for socials.
[04:19] Marco (Lumina): If you can include the benchmark chart that shows cost/latency pre/post that'd be helpful \u001f Daniel you have that, right?
[04:26] Daniel (Redwood): Yep I'll share the spreadsheet and a simplified chart.
[04:29] Aisha (Lumina): Also note the fallback policy \u001f we use a cheaper hosted variant as fallback during maintenance windows, that was important to keep SLAs up.
[04:40] Sofia (Redwood): Nice detail. Any tough lessons learned?
[04:43] Aisha (Lumina): Watch for prompt drift and schema changes in downstream systems, that bit bit us once \u001f added stricter input validation and a small human-in-loop step during edge cases.
[04:55] Daniel (Redwood): Good tip. For teams evaluating Redwood, what's the single biggest metric that mattered for Lumina?
[05:01] Marco (Lumina): For execs it was cost per completed summary and SLAs; for engineering it was p95 latency under concurrency. Both improved and that made the business case compelling.
[05:14] Sofia (Redwood): Okay switching gears a bit \u001f marketing questions: Elaine, any preferred quotes or disclaimers we should prep?
[05:21] Elaine (Lumina): Legal wants a short disclaimer about patient data redaction and that all PHI is removed from public excerpts. Also to confirm we won't disclose exact cost numbers.
[05:33] Priya (Redwood): We'll include that in the release doc. We can anonymize any patient-facing examples.
[05:39] Aisha (Lumina): Thanks, appreciate the caution.
[05:42] [06:00] Sofia (Redwood): Quick technical note \u001f Daniel can you mention the kernel/quantization tuning work?
[06:06] Daniel (Redwood): Sure, we tried a couple of quantization backends; the recommended kernel for the transformer variant gave us the best throughput on your GPU shape. Ended up with continuous batching and prefix cache to reduce repeated context cost.
[06:24] Marco (Lumina): That caching was a game-changer for repeated templated messages.
[06:30] Elaine (Lumina): Do you have any tips for other health orgs on rollout timing?
[06:34] Aisha (Lumina): Start with a low-risk workflow, instrument heavily, and get legal/security involved early \u001f saves time.
[06:42] Sofia (Redwood): Wrapping up \u001f any final quick soundbites for the episode?
[06:47] Aisha (Lumina): \"Redwood helped us scale automation while keeping patient safety central.\"
[06:53] Marco (Lumina): \"Predictable latency under realistic load was the turning point for us.\"
[06:58] Elaine (Lumina): \"Faster follow-up means better patient outcomes.\"
[07:03] Sofia (Redwood): Love those. We'll draft testimonial copy and send it to Aisha for approval.
[07:10] Priya (Redwood): Tentative publish window is early January 2026; we'll confirm after approvals.
[07:17] Aisha (Lumina): Works for us.
[07:20] Sofia (Redwood): Okay last housekeeping \u001f links and assets we'll share: benchmark spreadsheet, security packet, short bio blurbs. Anything else?
[07:28] Daniel (Redwood): I'll add the config snippets for batching and the quantization profile.
[07:33] Elaine (Lumina): We'll share a logo and preferred headshots.
[07:36] Sofia (Redwood): Perfect. Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the notes and next steps. End recording.
[07:45] [END] Note: occasional transcription imperfections \u001f some technical terms may be slightly off (e.g., kernel names, model family references).
